 ED raids seven locations in Telangana in Rs 326.49 crore bank fraud case
 Written By ZeeBiz WebTeam Published: 7:42 PM, Oct 23, 2026 | Updated: 7:42 PM, Oct 23, 2026 Officials said the searches were conducted at locations in Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Medchal-Malkajgiri under provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The search operation was carried out by the ED’s Hyderabad Zonal Office as part of an ongoing investigation. | ChatGPT generated/Representative Image The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday (October 23) carried out searches at seven premises in Telangana in connection with a case involving Kanakadhara Ventures Pvt Ltd (KVPL) and its directors over the alleged diversion of credit facilities worth Rs 326.49 crore.
 According to the ED, the credit facilities had been extended to the company by a consortium of banks led by Punjab National Bank.
 Officials said the searches were conducted at locations in Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Medchal-Malkajgiri under provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
 The search operation was carried out by the ED’s Hyderabad Zonal Office as part of an ongoing investigation into the alleged misuse of financial facilities sanctioned to KVPL.
 Alleged diversion through related entities 
 The agency said its investigation indicated that Bank Guarantee and Letter of Credit facilities provided to the company were allegedly misused.
 According to officials, funds were diverted through related and conduit entities using fabricated steel purchase invoices and transport documents.
 The ED also alleged that KVPL operated bank accounts outside the consortium arrangement without the knowledge of the lending banks.
 The alleged diversion of credit facilities amounting to Rs 326.49 crore is being examined as part of the agency’s money laundering investigation.
 Bank guarantees and letters of credit are commonly used by businesses to support commercial transactions and secure payments. The ED is looking into their alleged misuse as well as the movement of funds through intermediary entities.
 Officials said the searches were aimed at collecting evidence related to the alleged financial irregularities and tracing the flow of funds linked to the case.
 ED conducts searches across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Chandigarh 
 The ED has also conducted searches at 13 locations across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Chandigarh today, October 23, in connection with a money laundering case involving alleged fraudulent housing loans obtained in the name of Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) using forged documents, according to Zee Business sources.
 The ED's Delhi Zonal Office-II is carrying out the search operation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), in coordination with police and other security forces, sources said.
 The investigation relates to alleged irregularities in obtaining housing loans intended for NRIs through the use of forged documents. The agency is examining the suspected financial irregularities, the alleged role of the entities involved and the amount of the suspected fraud, sources said.
 During the searches, the ED may seize documents, digital evidence and other material relevant to the investigation, in accordance with the provisions of the law.
 The operation is aimed at gathering evidence related to the alleged offence and tracing the money suspected to be linked to it, sources added.
 BIS raids jewellery outlet in Amritsar 
 The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Jammu & Kashmir Branch Office carried out a search and seizure operation at a BIS-registered jewellery outlet in Partap Bazar, Chheharta, Amritsar, on October 22, 2026. During the inspection, BIS officials found hallmarking violations in several gold jewellery articles.
